name: Fertiliser supply
value: Egypt urea ~$535/t FOB; US ammonia +17% y/y
summary: Egyptian urea near $535 a tonne after gas cuts to fertiliser plants; US ammonia retail prices up 17% on a year
state: Egyptian granular urea fetched about $535 a tonne FOB in November contracts, up about 17% from about $457 in September, after gas supply to some plants was cut by 20% from 1 Nov (Fertilizer Daily, 9 Nov). In the US, retail anhydrous ammonia prices were up 17% on a year in early November and urea up 11% (UkrAgroConsult). No 60% three-month rise in urea, several exporters restricting at once, or closure of a key export route was found as of 19 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: Higher nitrogen fertiliser costs mainly affect farmers planning spring applications and can feed into food prices over the following year. No direct effect on household bills has been reported.
rubric_hit: Watch: Egypt gas cuts restrict a major urea exporter; urea ~+17% since Sept, below +60% three-month Alert line

sources.title: Fertilizer Daily — Egyptian urea price rises amid gas cuts
UkrAgroConsult — Anhydrous ammonia prices in the US rise 17%, urea up 11%

why: Fertiliser prices lead food prices by months; much of the world's urea and ammonia is exported from Russia, the Gulf and China.
drivers: Gas prices, Gulf shipping, export bans and quotas, sanctions, planting seasons.

rubric.alert: Urea up more than 60% in three months, several major exporters restricting at once, or a key export route closed.
rubric.watch: Urea up more than 30% in three months, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: Urea and ammonia prices within their normal range; no major export restrictions.
